newsitem.title: GREECE: GNN BOND GUIDE: INDEX-LINKED BONDS.
newsitem.headline: GNN BOND GUIDE: INDEX-LINKED BONDS.

text.p: This is the first in a series of brief presentations on different types of securities and financial instruments.
Responding to the request of some commercial banks, a brief description of indexed bonds follows.
Deputy Finance Minister Nikos Christodoulakis said Greece will issue CPI index-linked bonds at the end of February.

Index-linked bonds have their coupon payments or/and principal linked to a specific price index, usually the CPI index (the WPI index or commodity price indexes have also been used in some countries), providing a guaranteed real yield.
TYPES OF INDEXED BONDS
Index-linked bonds can be categorised into three broad types. (we ignore annuity bonds)
1) Coupon indexed bonds where coupon payments are adjusted for inflation
2) Principal indexed bonds where coupon payments and principal are adjusted for inflation
3) Zero-coupon bonds where there are no coupon payments and therefore only the principal is adjusted for inflation.
REASONS FOR ISSUING INDEX LINKED-BONDS
1) Attract more investors by offering a bigger menu of investment vehicles
2) Cut the cost of state borrowing by reducing substantially the risk premium related to the variability of inflation
3) Enhance the anti-inflationary credibility of the economic policy since the government has an incentive to fight inflation in order to slash its future cost of borrowing
4) Obtain a measure of inflationary expectations
5) Make long-term instruments more attractive by purging the inflation risk premium
6) Facilitate the execution of monetary policy by introducing more securities

Since the finance ministry has indicated that it tilts towards the zero-coupon indexed bonds we provide the main formulas for calculating the present value and redemption amount of these indexed zeros:
Please bear in mind that banks bid for the real yield at the auction and therefore the present value is a function of the real yield. (The Swedish pricing model is used)
Let P= present value
F= nominal value
r= real yield
I= index factor
where I= reference CPI index(settlement)/Base CPI Index
t= periods
K= Redemption amount
P= (I*F)/(1+r) raised to the power of (t)
K= F*(final CPI index/Base CPI index)
Please also note that different countries use different

time lags for the CPI index. Lags of one or more months are typically used. Also note that linear interpolation is used to calculate reference CPI indexes if settlement does not occur on the first day of the month.
The indexation lag could make the ex-post real yield
somewhat different from ex-ante real yield and therefore protection against inflation is not perfect.
The finance ministry provided its own formulas in
November which do not mention anything about time lags for the CPI index and do not treat the problem of dates within a month.
--Dimitris Kontogiannis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
